purpose: Locked exact known-answer test vectors for the PHYSICAL-CONSTANTS axis of the known-answer benchmark. Post-2019 SI redefinition (BIPM SI Brochure 9th ed., 2019) fixes the Avogadro number N_A, the Boltzmann constant k_B and the elementary charge e as EXACT defined integers, so the molar gas constant R = N_A*k_B and the Faraday constant F = N_A*e are exact RATIONAL products with no measurement uncertainty. This battery locks those constants (and the derived R*T, F/3600, and the sacrificial-zinc specific charge) that the portfolio's Arrhenius/Kissinger cure-kinetics, Eyring viscosity, and zinc galvanic modules silently depend on. Every expected value is an exact rational; no empirical fit; no candidate performance claim. AUDIT_ONLY.
scope: solvent-borne two-part epoxy-amine marine anti-corrosion coating physical-chemistry constants (Arrhenius/Kissinger cure, Eyring viscosity, sacrificial-zinc electrochemistry)

exact_defining_constants.zinc_standard_atomic_weight: 65.38 (IUPAC 2021 standard atomic weight of zinc; conventional, pinned)

tolerance_policy: Identity vectors (defining constants) PASS iff the independently reconstructed exact rational equals the pinned defining integer (exact equality; detects a typo/regression in a pinned constant). Derived vectors pin the expected value to the stated decimal places; the verifier re-derives the value as an EXACT product of raw defining constants (independent of any pinned R/F value -> non-circular) and PASSES iff round_half_up(exact_rational, decimals) equals the pinned expected. Float arithmetic never enters the gate.

fail_closed_hostile_vectors.trap: R = 8.314472 J/mol/K is the pre-2019 CODATA-2014 MEASURED value (with uncertainty). After the 2019 SI redefinition R is EXACTLY 8.314462618. Silently using the old measured R is a known-answer regression.
N_A = 6.022137e23 is an older (CODATA-1986-era) measured Avogadro number. The SI-2019 defined value is exactly 6.02214076e23.
Dropping the 0.15 K in the Celsius-to-Kelvin offset (using 273 instead of 273.15) is a common shortcut that biases every Arrhenius exponent.
F ~ 96500 C/mol is the textbook-rounded Faraday constant. Using it inflates sacrificial-zinc capacity by ~0.015%.
R = 1.987 cal/(mol K) is the gas constant in CALORIES; using it where Joules are required (or vice versa) is a units regression that changes every activation energy by the 4.184 cal->J factor.
